notes: Pictures show no per-stud detail, so all edges use null ports and each stacked piece is linked to representative pieces beneath it rather than every individual stud pair.

Step 4's four light-grey 1x6 plates are shown on the frame near the 4x6 plates; I joined them to the two light-grey 4x6 plates, which is an assumption.

Step 5's parts box shows 2 flat pieces and a 2x2 plate. I read these as the 2x 306926 tiles 1x2 and the 302226 plate 2x2 from the inventory. Their exact positions are assumed. The 2x2 plate is the base for the round-plate stack.

Element 614126 (black round plate 1x1) is listed in the catalogue as 'Wheel (black, small)' with only a pin-hole port. I used it as a small round plate that clips between the 2x2 round plates, with null ports.
4211480 (round tile 2x2, light grey) was not in the catalogue, so I added it as a new part type.

Step 18 sub-assembly: the picture is ambiguous. I assumed both 1x3 black plates sit on the top 1x3 brick. The white 1x3 plate goes on one, the 1x1 plate and 1x1 tile on the other, and the two antennas push onto studs of the white plate.
Step 12's 1x4 tile 243126 is placed on the 2x3 plates alongside the four jumper plates; its exact position is assumed.
Tower brick layers are chained in build order (steps 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17). Each brick is joined to representative pieces below it rather than every contacting piece.
